title: Telos
description: The end a venture exists to reach, at <venture>/purpose/telos.json (EE-023): start with the end. It states the end state, how anyone would know it was reached (measures), what the owners intend to happen when it is reached (owner outcome), and, for each phase of the Succession Matrix, the exit criteria that must be true to leave it, each serving at least one measure. Other layers read it instead of asking again: the governance layer's exit.json prefers the owner outcome's path, and MAD's governance tier takes its success measure from the primary measure. packages/naive/src/checks/check-telos.mjs checks it. Written by the owner; an agent may draft it but not settle it.

statement.description: The end, in one sentence: what the venture is for when it has done its job

end_state.description: What is true in the world when the end is reached

horizon.description: The year the end should be reached by, or 'open'

kind.description: The kind of measure; the first six match MAD's success_measure answers, impact is a change in the world beyond the venture

path.description: What the owners intend to happen once the end is reached; hold means they keep it

serves.description: Measure ids this criterion moves the venture toward

evidence.description: How it is shown: a check command, an evidence record, or a metric

met.description: Set when a person says the criterion is met (naive phase --meet); the gate to the next phase passes when every criterion of the current phase has it

by.description: The person who said it is met

evidence.description: What shows it: a record, a metric, a check

phases.description: Per phase, what must be true to leave it; refines that phase's generic gate in packages/naive/src/functions/products/frameworks/product-anatomy/phases.json for this venture

steering.description: How the venture decides to start, keep going or stop, when it reviews that, and what happens when evidence says the direction is wrong (EE-040; MAD's governance tier reads these as go_decision, review_cadence and change_of_direction). Who may make each call is in the decision rights: continue-or-stop and change-direction.

go_decision.description: test-hypotheses-first: assumptions are written down and tested with real people before committing. business-case-upfront: a case is approved before work starts. owner-judgment: the owner decides as they go. last-responsible-moment: commitments wait until delay costs more than deciding.

review.description: When the decision to continue is reviewed: after each experiment or customer test, at each release or milestone, on a calendar, continuously from watched measures, or never formally

review_period.description: For fixed-period: the period, such as quarterly

change_of_direction.description: pivot-on-evidence: changing the product, customer or model is expected and planned for. formal-change-control: a change request the deciders approve or reject. owner-decides: the owner adjusts as they see fit. public-proposal: anyone proposes in public and maintainers decide by a published rule.
